description: Seventeen individual open-web queries (402 rendered result headers) searched Bosnia-wide and focused on Sarajevo, Banja Luka, Zenica and continuity, in Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian Latin, Serbian Cyrillic and English. Searches surfaced women’s, journalists’, miners’ and OHR-related events; they did not systematically cover every canton, district, sector, archive or local-language outlet. Coverage is bounded, not exhaustive.
required_followup: Continue region- and sector-specific local reporting searches for March 2023, especially Tuzla, Mostar, Bihać, Travnik and other Federation/RS centers and public-service, student, farmer and pensioner actions; no claim that unobserved events did not occur.

description: The actual 8 March Banja Luka women’s march and demands are reported by two opened sources, but neither gives a simultaneous attendance count. The march remains pending threshold.
required_followup: Seek a contemporaneous organizer or local report with a defensible count at this single march.

description: The 9 March Sarajevo activists’ gathering outside SDP headquarters is reported as “više desetina osoba,” while the other report’s “tens” refers to letter signatures. Neither establishes 50 participants simultaneously. Its immediate recipient was the party over a candidate for a cantonal minister; the government-policy target remains ambiguous.
required_followup: Locate contemporaneous attendance estimate and a source clarifying whether protesters demanded action by a domestic government/appointment authority or solely SDP party withdrawal.

description: The miners’ public episode has a qualifying crowd on 28 March and another several-hundred gathering on 30 March; a one-hour workplace warning strike occurred on 29 March. The 30 March account says miners would not disperse before a mayoral commitment, while the council decision still needed the mayor’s signature. Final closure and resolution are unreported.
required_followup: Use permitted contemporaneous local/union/city records after 30 March to establish whether the mayor signed, when miners dispersed, and whether the same protest episode continued into April.

description: The 31 March OHR gathering had several hundred attendees, but reports identify the immediate target as the international OHR/High Representative, while also citing possible effects on Federation constitutional/election policy and broad democracy/human-rights demands. Eligibility as a protest targeting the domestic state or policy remains unresolved.
required_followup: Seek explicit contemporaneous statements identifying a domestic Bosnia authority/policy as a target, and distinguish those from demands directed to OHR/Christian Schmidt.

description: The N1 live report says at 15:08 that attendees were beginning to disperse, not that all had left or the protest had ended. The 31 March event end date is unknown.
required_followup: Find an explicit close-time or retrospective statement that the full OHR protest ended; do not infer closure from partial dispersal.

description: The exact Klix OHR protest article URL returned HTTP 403; the attempt and receipt are retained, no retry or alternate URL was attempted. Other permitted RFE, Federalna and N1 reports provide event evidence, so this denial does not by itself block the candidate’s source coverage.
required_followup: No follow-up needed unless an independently discovered, permitted source materially resolves an open field; do not retry the denied exact URL.

description: A 30 March Klix article says about 1,000 miners protested “yesterday,” whereas the Klix 28 March article and the RFE 30 March retrospective explicitly date the about-1,000 crowd to 28 March; a separate 29 March warning strike is also reported. The relative-date wording may be stale or refer to a different action, but available body evidence does not resolve it. The 28 March onset/threshold is based only on the explicitly dated S013 report and not shifted by the ambiguous “yesterday” reference.
required_followup: Seek another contemporaneous local account or original union/city record that distinguishes the 28 March crowd, 29 March warning strike and 30 March gathering, and clarify the “yesterday” reference.
